value: in Y-tube olfactometer bioassays only four of seven EAG-active synthetic plant volatiles (m-xylene, butyl acrylate, butyl propionate, butyl butyrate) elicited positive behavioural responses from adults
units: categorical (Y-tube choice versus mineral-oil solvent, chi-squared goodness-of-fit)

source.authors: Hongsheng Pan, Yanhui Lu, Chunli Xiu, Huihui Geng, Xiaoming Cai, Xiaoling Sun, Yongjun Zhang, Livy Williams III, Kris A. G. Wyckhuys, Kongming Wu
source.title: Volatile fragrances associated with flowers mediate host plant alternation of a polyphagous mirid bug

method: behavioural: single-insect Y-tube olfactometer; each synthetic compound (10 ul of a 1 ug/ul dilution, i.e. 10 ug, on a 5 x 0.5 cm filter paper) against mineral oil solvent; 60 adults per gender per compound
conditions: Unmated 6 to 8 day old adults, from bugs collected in cotton fields at Langfang (Hebei, China) and reared on green bean pods and 10 % sucrose. Seven compounds were EAG-active in flowering-plant headspace (EAG on 10 individuals per sex per compound). Y-tube results by sex: m-xylene female P = 0.036, male P = 0.039; butyl acrylate female P = 0.003, male P = 0.010; butyl propionate female P = 0.014, male P = 0.022; butyl butyrate female P = 0.001, male P = 0.002. Results: no difference between genders for any of the seven compounds (P > 0.05). The three other EAG-active compounds, (Z)-3-hexen-1-ol, (Z)-3-hexenyl acetate and 3-ethylbenzaldehyde, were not attractive in the Y-tube; their P values, and percentages choosing each arm and chi-squared values, were not read. The paper does not say whether Y-tube arms were swapped or assigned at random. Not a sensitivity measure: single dose, no detection threshold or non-detection disclosure. Same paper: in greenhouse cages and field bucket traps the four compounds caught more bugs than solvent controls.
quote: Although the adults responded to all seven synthetic plant volatiles in electroantennography tests, only four (m-xylene, butyl acrylate, butyl propionate and butyl butyrate) elicited positive behavioral responses in Y-tube olfactometer bioassays.
note: Sentence read whole in three abutting pieces and both neighbouring sentences seen, so both ends are verified. Family and order from the paper's Abstract and Introduction ('Hemiptera: Miridae'). value: male and female adults showed positive chemotaxis in Y-tube tests toward volatiles from Cinnamomum camphora and negative chemotaxis toward volatiles from C. chekiangensis or Phoebe chekiangensis
units: categorical (Y-tube response rate versus air control, chi-squared)

source.authors: Cong Chen, Zhaoyan Lin, Jingyi Du, Jingyi Huang, Chunmei Ling, Jianfeng Chen
source.title: Olfactory Selection Preferences of Pagiophloeus tsushimanus (Coleoptera: Curculionidae) Adults Toward Lauraceae Plants

method: behavioural: glass Y-tube olfactometer (4 cm inner diameter, 20 cm arms at 60 degrees, 40 cm main arm, 300 mL/min airflow); five two-year-old twigs of about 10 cm per arm against an empty-bottle air control; three repetitions of 12 adults (6 female, 6 male) per comparison; arms reversed after each test
conditions: Results section 3.3.1 against air: C. camphora attracted females (chi2 = 5.974, p < 0.01) and males (chi2 = 4.010, p < 0.05); females did not respond to C. chekiangensis (chi2 = 0.724) or P. chekiangensis (chi2 = 1.290) twigs (both p > 0.05). Larvae and pupae collected from 15-year-old camphor trees in southern China (sites and dates not given) and reared in the laboratory; adults emerging on the same day were selected and starved 24 h. Tested at 2000 lx, 26 +/- 1 C; time of day not stated; arm reversal described but no randomisation procedure. Same Results section 3.3.1: males responded significantly less to C. chekiangensis and P. chekiangensis twigs than to air (the male chi2 is printed as 4.010 for both, which looks like a reporting error), and plant-versus-plant tests preferred C. camphora over both (e.g. females v C. chekiangensis chi2 = 11.227) with C. chekiangensis against P. chekiangensis null (females chi2 = 0.502, males chi2 = 0.020); no sex differences were significant. The Abstract sentence quoted says both sexes had a negative chemotaxis to the two other species, which the female nulls in Results do not show. Single-compound Y-tube tests (section 3.5): linalool attracted both sexes (chi2 = 6.237 and 4.163, p < 0.05), beta-caryophyllene was null (chi2 = 1.147 and 1.029), alpha-phellandrene and trans-nerolidol were avoided by both sexes. Choice and no-choice feeding tests: both sexes fed most on C. camphora, with C. chekiangensis and P. chekiangensis not differing from each other. Odour preference at one distance, not a detection threshold.
quote: The Y-shaped olfactometer experiments and electroantennography measurements results showed that male and female adults of P. tsushimanus had a positive chemotaxis towards volatiles released by C. camphora and a negative chemotaxis towards volatiles released by C. chekiangensis or P. chekiangensis.
note: Sentence read whole in three abutting pieces (start and end seen); the chi-squared figures in conditions come from Results section 3.3.1, read in pieces, and are not part of the quote. Family and order from the paper (title and Taxonomy line: Coleoptera: Curculionidae).
